title: Responsive Web Design
description: Learn how to build layouts that work on any screen size.

sections.title: Mobile-First & the Viewport
sections.content: Responsive design means a page reflows to fit different screen sizes. Mobile-first means designing for small screens first, then enhancing the layout for larger screens. The viewport meta tag tells the browser to match the page width to the device width instead of using a fixed desktop viewport.

quiz.question: What does responsive design allow a webpage to do?
What does mobile-first design mean?
choices: Designing for small screens first, then enhancing for larger screens
Testing mobile devices after desktop devices

quiz.question: What is the purpose of the viewport meta tag?
choices: To add animations to a webpage
To control how the page is displayed on different devices

sections.title: Media Queries
sections.content: Media queries apply CSS rules only when certain conditions are met, such as a minimum screen width. They allow you to change layouts, font sizes, spacing, and other styles at different breakpoints.

quiz.question: What is a media query used for?
choices: Applying CSS styles based on certain conditions

quiz.question: What does a breakpoint represent in responsive design?
choices: A screen width where the layout or styles can change

quiz.question: Which media query applies styles when the viewport is at least 768 pixels wide?

sections.title: Flexible Layouts (Flexbox & Grid)
sections.content: Flexbox arranges items in a single row or column and distributes space between them. CSS Grid arranges items in rows and columns at the same time. Relative units such as %, em, rem, vw, and vh can scale more flexibly than fixed pixel values.

Which CSS layout system is designed for two-dimensional rows and columns?
Which unit is relative to the viewport width?

exam.question: Why is responsive design important?

It prevents users from resizing their browser

exam.question: What is a media query?
choices: A CSS mechanism for applying styles under specific conditions

exam.question: What is a breakpoint?

A screen condition where responsive styles can change

exam.question: Why are media queries useful in responsive web design?

They remove the need for CSS
They prevent webpages from loading on mobile devices
